text:
"May you receive the undivided love of your husband," the holy women said to Uma, who was bowed in humility. But by her, who eventually shared half of his body, even the blessings of her beloved kin were surpassed. <note>verse 28</note>

The humble and prostrate Uma was told by those virtuous women: "May you obtain the unbroken <note>original: akhaṇḍitam</note> and uninjured love of your husband, Shiva." The use of the grammatical particle <term>sma</term> here indicates the past tense. By Gauri, who went on to share half of the body <note>original: ardha-śarīra-bhājā</note> of Shiva, even the blessings of her affectionate relatives <note>original: snigdha-jana</note> were surpassed or set aside. This is because she attained a result even greater than what they had wished for.

The Mountain, having skillfully completed every task according to his desires and his wealth, stood in the assembly hall occupied by his friends, waiting for the arrival of the one who has a bull as his emblem <note>Shiva</note>. <note>verse 29</note>

The skillful Himavan <note>the personified Himalaya mountains and father of Parvati</note>, having finished all the duties for Parvati’s wedding in a manner fitting his resolve and his great power, stood waiting. He was in the assembly <note>original: sabhāyām</note> surrounded by his kinsmen, looking out for the arrival of Shiva <note>literally "the one whose sign is a bull"</note>.

Meanwhile, on the mountain of Kubera <note>Mount Kailasa</note>, the Mothers who had been summoned respectfully placed before the Destroyer of the City the ornaments and attire suitable for his upcoming marriage. <note>verse 30</note>

At the same time that Parvati was being adorned, on Mount Kailasa, the materials for decoration <note>original: prasādhanam</note> and wedding ornaments suitable for the marriage were set out. These were placed before Bhava <note>Shiva</note>, also known as the Destroyer of the City <note>Tripura</note>, by the Seven Mothers <note>the Matrikas, such as Brahmi and others</note> who had been respectfully invited.

<summary>This page describes Parvati receiving blessings for a successful marriage and her father Himavan preparing for the wedding procession, while Shiva is simultaneously attended to by the Divine Mothers on Mount Kailasa.</summary>
<keywords>Parvati, Shiva, Himavan, marriage blessings, Mount Kailasa, Matrikas, Kumarasambhava, Kalidasa</keywords>
